transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

Well, I guess... it's probably just a small thing, really. Nothing too serious, I hope. But, um, what brings me in is that... well, I spend a lot of time down at the museum, and lately, people there will be talking right to me, maybe about the next art walk or something, and I’ll be looking right at them, nodding along... but then I realize I somehow completely missed the middle part of what they just said. 

I always feel terrible having to ask them to run it by me again. It's a bit embarrassing, honestly, to be my age and making people repeat themselves. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information to start with.
Do you also have trouble hearing people in other situations, like in noisy rooms or when someone speaks from another room?

Oh, um... no, actually. My hearing itself seems to be perfectly fine, thankfully. Even if it's noisy or someone is calling from the kitchen, I can hear the sounds without any trouble. 

I actually went and had my ears checked a little while ago, just to make sure I wasn't making a fuss over nothing, you know? I didn't want to waste anyone's time if all I needed was a hearing aid. But the doctor there said my hearing is great for a guy my age. So it's not the volume... it's just that the words sort of slip away from me even when it's quiet and they're right in front of me. 

I hope I'm explaining that okay? I know you have to ask about all the possibilities, so I hope that helps narrow it down a little.
When someone is speaking to you, do you understand the words themselves, or do they sometimes sound like gibberish?

Oh, no, definitely not gibberish. I understand the words just fine, thankfully. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, completely losing my grip on things! 

The words make perfect sense when people are saying them. It's really just... well, my attention just sort of takes a little detour, I suppose. I hear the words, and I know exactly what they mean, but then I just realize I wasn't really absorbing the whole thought. 

Does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you the details you actually need.
When you read written text, do you ever have trouble understanding what the words mean?

Oh, no, no trouble like that at all. Reading is... well, it's perfectly fine. I know I only went through high school, but I've always understood what I'm reading. The words themselves make total sense. 

I really hope I'm not making it sound like my brain is turning to mush or anything! It's really just that little focus thing I mentioned when people are talking to me. But reading a book or, you know, a placard down at the museum... no, I understand the meaning of the written words just fine. 

Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way and not leading you down the wrong path.
Do you ever have trouble understanding what people say to you, even when you can hear them clearly?

Oh, no, not at all. I think... well, it's a lot like what I was trying to say a moment ago, though maybe I didn't do the best job explaining it! I understand what people are telling me just fine. The meaning is all there, and I definitely don't have any trouble grasping what they're trying to communicate to me. 

It's really just that little issue of my attention drifting off, rather than not actually comprehending them. I hope I'm not making this more complicated than it needs to be? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know and not confusing the issue.
Do you ever have trouble finding the right words when you’re speaking?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. Finding words is... well, it's usually pretty easy for me. I can hold a conversation just fine, and I don't really find myself grasping for what to say or anything like that. 

I mean, everyone forgets a name or a specific word every now and then, right? But nothing out of the ordinary. I really don't want you to think I'm having trouble communicating or, you know, losing my vocabulary! I'm pretty articulate, I think. 

Does that help clear that up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
When someone speaks to you, do you ever have trouble understanding what the words mean?

No, no, I understand the words perfectly. It's really just like I was saying before... the words themselves make total sense. I just, you know, sometimes my mind wanders off while they're talking. 

But I definitely know what the words mean! I'm not having any trouble with my hearing or my understanding, I promise. I really hope I'm making sense and not just repeating myself too much. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is this all helpful for you?
Have you ever been told you have trouble hearing, or needed a hearing test before this started?

Oh, no, definitely not. My hearing is actually quite good, I think. I've never had anyone tell me I couldn't hear them, and I haven't ever needed to go in for a hearing test or anything like that. 

I'm pretty sure everything is working just fine in that department! It really all just comes back to the attention thing, not my ears. I hope that's the right kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm not leading you down the wrong path with all this.
Do you avoid social situations because you fear being judged or embarrassed by other people?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I like being around people! I don't avoid socializing or anything like that. I don't really worry about people judging me... at least, not any more than the average person does, right? 

I might sometimes be a little quiet if I lose the thread of a conversation, but it's not because I'm scared of being embarrassed. I just sort of... drift a bit. But I still go out and see folks, and I enjoy it. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a hermit or anything! I'm pretty normal when it comes to being around others, I think. Does that make sense?
When you’re around other people, do you ever feel nervous that they’re watching or evaluating you?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't feel like I'm under a microscope or anything when I'm out and about. I'm just a regular guy, you know? 

I might get a little self-conscious if I realize I've completely zoned out while someone was talking directly to me, but it's not like I'm sitting there worrying that everyone is staring at me or judging my every move. I just try to be polite and pleasant. I hope that's the kind of thing you're asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here.
Do you avoid speaking up in groups because you’re afraid of being judged or embarrassed?

No, I wouldn't say I avoid speaking up. I mean, I'm not the loudest guy in the room, but I'm happy to chime in when I have something to say. 

I guess sometimes I hold back just a little if I'm not entirely sure what the topic is—like if my mind wandered and I missed a detail, I don't want to say something silly. But it's not a fear of being judged, really. It's just trying to be considerate and not interrupt the flow, you know? I think most people do that. I hope that's a normal way to handle it? I just try to be a good listener when I'm in a group.
Do you ever forget appointments, errands, or conversations in your day-to-day life?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I'm 63 now and retired, so my schedule isn't exactly packed, but I'm pretty good about keeping track of my errands and appointments. I'd really hate to inconvenience anyone by just not showing up, you know? 

I mean, sure, maybe I'll forget to grab a specific item at the grocery store once in a blue moon, or a little detail of a chat might slip my mind, but nothing major. Just the normal amount for a guy my age, I think. I try to be really responsible about that sort of thing. I hope that sounds about right to you? I definitely wouldn't say it's a problem.
When you’re in social situations, do you feel a strong fear that other people will judge you negatively?

Oh, um, no, not at all. I mean, I think I'm pretty comfortable around folks. I don't really worry about them thinking poorly of me or anything like that. 

I just try to be friendly and treat everyone with respect, and I figure if I do that, there's no reason for anyone to judge me, right? I mean, maybe sometimes I worry a tiny bit if I've been quiet for a while because I lost track of the conversation... I just don't want anyone to think I'm being rude or ignoring them. But it's not a strong fear or anything. Just wanting to be a good neighbor, really. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I hope I'm answering these questions okay for you.
When you’re in social situations, do you feel a strong fear of being judged or embarrassed by other people?

No, I don't think so. I mean, you just asked something similar, right? I hope I didn't confuse you with my last answer. But no, I don't feel a strong fear of being embarrassed or judged. 

I'm just a regular guy, you know? I try to be polite and go with the flow. If I do get a little quiet because my mind drifted off, I just hope folks don't think I'm being standoffish. But I definitely don't sit there terrified of what they're thinking. I just want to make sure everyone's having a nice time. I think I handle social things pretty normally... at least, I hope I do? Does that make sense?
Do you ever get lost or feel confused in places that used to be familiar to you?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I don't get lost. I've lived around here for years, so I know my way around pretty well. 

I mean, sure, if they go and change the layout of the grocery store, I might have to wander down an extra aisle or two to find the coffee, but that happens to everyone, right? It's not like I'm wandering the streets not knowing where I am or anything scary like that. I'm completely fine driving to the hardware store or the post office. My memory for places is still sharp, I promise. I really hope you don't think I'm losing my marbles or anything... I'm doing okay, aren't I?
Have other people noticed that your memory is getting worse?

Oh, no, no one's said anything like that. My wife, she might tease me sometimes if I forget to take the trash out on Tuesday morning, but... well, that's just me getting distracted with something else, you know? It's not my memory failing. 

I mean, everyone forgets little things here and there, especially at my age, right? But nobody's ever sat me down and told me they're worried about my memory. I try really hard to keep on top of things so I don't let anyone down. I'm still doing my part around the house and all. I hope that's the right answer... I'm doing alright, don't you think?
Have you started avoiding social events because you’re worried you might say or do something embarrassing?

Oh, no, I haven't done that. I still go to things... barbecues, church events, that sort of stuff. I like seeing folks. 

I mean, I guess sometimes I might be a little quiet if there's a lot going on and I can't quite keep track of the conversation, but I don't stay home just because I'm worried about embarrassing myself. I try to be good company. If I drift off for a second, people usually just think I'm being a good listener, you know? I don't think I've ever done anything truly embarrassing that would make me want to hide away. I always try to make sure I'm not a bother to anyone. That sounds normal, right? I'm not doing anything wrong by just being a little quiet sometimes, am I?
Have you had any difficulty managing your finances?

Oh, no, I manage things just fine. I mean, my wife usually handles the day-to-day bills, but that's just because she's always been better with numbers, not because I can't do it. 

If I need to run to the bank or pay for something at the hardware store, I don't have any trouble. Sometimes I might take a second longer to double-check my change, just to be careful, but I've never overdrawn the account or forgotten to pay the mortgage or anything terrible like that. We're doing okay on our retirement savings, and I make sure we don't spend more than we should. I try to be really responsible with our money. That's a good thing, right? I'm not doing too bad for a guy my age, am I?
Have you noticed your memory getting worse over time?

No, I wouldn't say it's getting worse. I mean, my memory is as good as it's ever been, really. 

Sure, I might walk into a room and forget what I went in there for, but everyone does that, right? It's just a normal part of getting older. It's not like I'm forgetting important things, like people's names or how to get home. I try to keep my mind sharp, you know, doing crosswords and reading the paper. I think I'm doing pretty well for my age, don't you? I mean, a little forgetfulness here and there is nothing to worry about, is it?
Have you started avoiding social situations because you’re afraid people will judge or embarrass you?

Oh, um, I think you might have asked me something real similar to that just a few minutes ago, actually. But, uh, no, my answer is still the same. I don't avoid going out at all. 

Like I was saying before, I really do enjoy being around folks. I always try to be polite and mind my manners, so there's really no reason for anyone to judge me or think badly of me, you know? I just sit back and listen if the conversation gets a little too fast for me to follow. People don't mind that, do they? I figure as long as I'm smiling and being friendly, I'm doing alright. That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
